title: Lettre Tate (mai 66) (Cristaux) : lettre (1966), tapuscrit (s.d.), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is from the typescript of Grothendieck's May 1966 letter to Tate on crystals, section 1.10–1.11.

Setting. S is a scheme of characteristic p. Crystals are absolute crystals over S of some species F, a fibred category over (Sch). frob_S is the absolute Frobenius and M^(p) = frob_S^* M.

1. Two Frobenius structures.
- A p-crystal is a crystal M with F: M^(p) -> M.
- A p^{-1}-crystal is a crystal M with V: M -> M^(p).
- A cartesian contravariant functor between fibred categories, such as duality M -> M^vee, exchanges the two notions.
- Both kinds are stable under tensor operations.

2. Bicrystals (Dieudonné crystals). When F is fibred in additive categories, a bicrystal of weight 1, also called a 'cristal de Dieudonné', is a crystal with both F and V such that FV = p and VF = p. The typescript says VF = id; see errors. This is meant to model families of Dieudonné modules, i.e. formal / p-divisible groups, or 'H^1_dR'.

3. Weight i. For higher degree i, a bicrystal of weight i satisfies FV = p^i and VF = p^i. This is what F and V look like on torsion-free crystalline H^i of a smooth proper variety: V = p^i F^{-1}.

4. Tate objects. The Tate bicrystal T^i is the unit crystal O_T with F = V = p^i. It has weight 2i, which is the handwritten correction 'poids 2i'. T^i is the i-th tensor power of T^1. Weights add under tensor product.

5. Inverting T^1 (§1.11). The category of crystals of modules is Z_p-linear. Inverting T^1, where F = p, forces inverting p, i.e. localization.
- This means passing to the Serre quotient by the thick subcategory of p-torsion objects (equivalently all torsion objects).
- The handwritten note says this amounts to keeping the objects and taking Hom ⊗_Z Q.
- The result is the category of isocrystals ('cristaux à isogénie près') over S.
- The next page builds p-isocristaux and bi-isocristaux (F an isomorphism) from this. It also builds fully faithful functors Bicr(S,i) -> Bicr(S,i+1), (M,F,V) |-> (M,F,pV), after localization.

The purpose is a crystalline replacement for ℓ-adic coefficients: Dieudonné theory in families, Tate twists, and an isogeny category with duality.
errors: Weight-1 relation is typed VF = id_{M^(p)}. It should be VF = p·id_{M^(p)}, as the weight-i formula on the same page shows. This is a typo.

The text first says Tate bicrystal 'de poids i', then hand-corrects it to 2i (F = V = p^i gives FV = p^{2i}). It then calls T^1 'le bicristal de Tate de poids 1', although T^1 has weight 2. This is an index/weight slip.

The Serre quotient by torsion objects is described as 'same objects, Hom ⊗ Q'. That holds for finitely presented (Noetherian-type) objects, not for arbitrary crystals of modules. The next page itself restricts duality to objects of finite type. This is a small unstated hypothesis.

missed.claim: The weight-i bicrystal is defined with an integral V satisfying FV = VF = p^i, as a structure in its own right. Over a base S (not just a perfect point), this anticipates the integral 'F-V' and weight formalism later used for crystalline cohomology, de Rham–Witt and Ekedahl. Those later notions are usually not traced to this letter. However, the letter is well known and cited, so this is attribution nuance rather than a missed result.
missed.quote: il y a lieu d'introduire la notion de bi-cristal de poids i , qui est un cristal muni de F et V satisfaisant aux relations FV = p^i id_M , VF = p^i id_M(p)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor historical attribution for integral weight-i Frobenius/Verschiebung structures. Mathematically it is now standard.

deep.surprise_reason: This is the well-known 1966 letter to Tate introducing crystals and isocrystals, which is widely cited. The content (Dieudonné crystals, Tate twists, isogeny category) is foundational and fully absorbed into the literature. The only mild point is the early explicit weight-i bicrystal notion with integral V over a base.
transcription_corrections: The weight-1 relation reads 'VF = id_{M(p)}' in the image, as transcribed. This is a typo in the original (should be p·id), not a transcription error.
The circled marginal '2i' sits beside the 'Par exemple' line. 'poids 2i' and 'qui' (typed over 'qi') are manual corrections.
The page number '7' in the top right corner is handwritten; the archive page '8' is at bottom left.
In the handwritten footnote, 'Hom ⊗_Z Q' has the Z written as a double-struck/underlined Z under the ⊗.
